adds.title: 2023 court testimony of trans women survivors of dictatorship blacksite
adds.summary: In 2023 trans women survivors testified in court that during Argentina's dictatorship they were held in secret prisons where they suffered severe abuse.

adds.title: BBC Mundo report 2014 - 'Argentina leads the trans revolution in the world'
adds.summary: Argentina enacted the Gender Identity Law in 2012 as the world's first law permitting change of name on all official documents without judicial process or psychological certification and guaranteeing free hormonal treatments and surgical interventions through public and private healthcare, and by May 2014 over half of the trans population had updated their DNI including a 6-year-old in October 2013 as the first minor recognized without judicial process, with increased access to health, education, work and civil-political rights, physical mistreatment and sexual abuse of detained trans women falling from 48.3% and 43% before the law to under 10% after, avoidance of health centers for fear of discrimination falling from nearly half to 5.3% with hospital placement by affirmed gender and name, a publicly funded Casa Trans scheduled to open in December 2014 in Caballito, Buenos Aires and the Mocha Celis school in Chacarita serving as trans educational refuge alongside a proposed tax exemption for firms hiring trans workers, while formal employment exclusion persisted with most trans women limited to sex work, 5 in 10 trans men reporting suicidal ideation and 4 in 10 reporting attempts, life expectancy at 35 years, and continued family expulsion and hostile treatment in more machista provinces.
